_comment: Configuration for tools/market-intelligence.mjs — the daily European market scan.
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR
Everything the scan decides with lives here rather than in the generator: the
query pools per market, how much a source is trusted, how a candidate is
scored, and the thresholds that turn a score into an action. An argument about
what the engine publishes is therefore an argument about this file.
THE RULE THE WHOLE ENGINE RUNS ON
The engine may not invent. Not a municipality, not a project, not a permit,
not a price, not a contact, and above all not a source URL. When there is
nothing real to publish it records NO_PUBLISH and publishes nothing. A day
with no news is a normal day; a day with invented news is a broken site.
SEARCH IS NOT CONFIGURED BY DEFAULT
There is no search API key in this repository and there must not be one — the
standing rule is that no secret is committed. Without MODUNERA_SEARCH_PROVIDER
and its key in the environment, the scan runs, finds nothing, and reports
NO_PUBLISH with the reason 'provider not configured'. That is the honest
failure mode, and it is loud rather than silent.
QUERIES ARE PER MARKET AND PER LANGUAGE
A German municipal signal is not found by searching in English. Each market
carries its own terms in its own language, which is also why the results are
worth having.

run.schedule_note: 04:35 UTC is 07:35 Europe/Istanbul. Istanbul is UTC+3 all year, so this does not drift with daylight saving. It runs before the daily post at 05:12 UTC on purpose: the scan may add a news item, and the post run should pick it up in the same morning rather than the next one. It is not on the hour because GitHub schedules cluster at :00 and are delayed there most.

queries.q: Tiny House Ferienanlage Tourismus Gemeinde Schweiz
tiny house commune permis de construire Suisse

source_authority.note: Municipality, canton, national government, official planning or participation portal, procurement portal, EU institution.
Reputable national or regional media, architecture and construction trade press, professional associations.
Everything not matched above. Usable as a lead to an official source, never as the source itself.

blocked_as_primary_source.note: Never accepted as the source of a regulation, permit or project status. May be used to find the official source, which is then cited instead.

scoring.note: Section 27 of the master prompt. A candidate is only considered for publication above publish_threshold.

quality_gate.note: Section 55. Checked before anything is written, not after.

commercial_signals.note: Section 28. These raise the commercial opportunity score because they are the developments that turn into an enquiry.

status_taxonomy.note: Section 23. Assigned only from a verified source; anything else is UNKNOWN.

_note: Sections 37 and 38. There is no live Search Console connection and there
cannot be one from a public repository, so the engine reads an export the
owner drops in: data/gsc-export.json (API shape, {rows:[...]}), or the CSV
files from the Search Console UI's own Export button, unzipped into
data/gsc/. Column headings are matched in English and Turkish, because the
export carries the interface language of whoever downloaded it.
The thresholds below are policy, not physics. They are here so changing
them is an edit to a data file and not to the engine.
render_note: /intelligence/ is unlisted, not secret: anyone who types the URL sees it.
Your Search Console queries are the list of what you rank for and what you
nearly rank for, which is exactly what a competitor would like. So the page
shows only how many opportunities were found in each bucket, and the
queries themselves stay in build-report-market-intelligence.txt and
data/market-signals.json. Set this to true only if you have decided that
publishing the query list is acceptable.

high_impression_low_ctr.action: title and meta description are the test; the page already ranks

near_page_one.action: strengthen the page that already ranks, do not mint a second one

missing_content.action: impressions exist and no page answers the query; a new page is worth considering

country_growth.action: the cluster for that market is working; strengthen it

decision.note: Section 18. Creating a new URL is deliberately the last option, not the default.
decision.location_pages_note: Section 19. 14,641 programmatic location pages already exist and are held out of the sitemap by data/location-index-policy.json. The engine may never add one. A place-specific finding updates the existing page for that place or becomes a news item; it does not mint a URL.
decision.cannibalisation_note: Section 39. A candidate whose title overlaps an existing indexed page above this is routed to UPDATE, never to CREATE.
decision.find_official_source_note: Section 14, OFFICIAL SOURCE FIRST. A newspaper reporting that a municipality is planning a tiny-house site is a lead, not the source. The first live scan returned NDR reporting on a Schleswig-Holstein Baugebiet and the engine wanted to publish it; what it should do is keep it as a lead so a person finds the municipality's own page and cites that. Tier 2 above the threshold gets this action, never CREATE_NEWS.
decision.store_policy: Only candidates the decision engine did not reject are kept. The first live scan produced 215 signals of which 208 were tier 3 classifieds, auction listings and holiday-park directories; storing those forever would add roughly two hundred rows a day and bury the seven that matter. Rejections are counted in the run, not kept.
decision.verify_on_source_note: Section 56. A search result is a title, a URL and a snippet. It is not enough to write an article from, and the engine must never fill the gap. The first live scan wanted to publish a district's tender INDEX page as a project, because tier 1 plus a good score was all it took. So a candidate the scan found is never published directly: at best it becomes VERIFY_ON_SOURCE, which means a person opens the page and, if it holds a real project, writes it into data/verified-signals-inbox.json. Only a candidate that came through that inbox — that a person has actually read — can reach CREATE_NEWS.

auto_publish.note: Section 65. Read from the environment at run time; these are the defaults when unset.
auto_publish.why: Every default is false. A regulation or permit statement that reaches this site without a person reading it first is the one failure this project cannot absorb, and the site already carries the reputation of being the careful supplier.

_note: Section 15 and 74. The adapter for the search provider named in
MODUNERA_SEARCH_PROVIDER. No key is here and none may be: it comes from the
environment, as a GitHub Actions repository secret in CI.
Brave's 'Search' plan is the one this is written against - $5 per 1,000
requests with $5 of credit applied monthly, which at 28 requests a day is
roughly the whole bill. The 'Answers' plan is deliberately not used: it
returns a written summary, and a summary is not a source you can verify.

brave.freshness_note: pm = the last 31 days. The scan looks for what changed, not for what is on the web.
brave.retry_note: Brave's documentation does not enumerate the supported country codes, so a market whose code it rejects is retried once without the country parameter instead of being lost.
